I'd like to maintain a high standard of quality on this sub, and one of the more important things I'd like to tackle is made-up bs explanations that "sound good so they must be true".

This kind of stuff is rampant on sites like reddit and tumblr where there's a long explanation that sounds like it could be true, and thus it's regarded as truth. This misinformation spreads.

So, I'm asking: Should explanations that don't cite reliable sources be against the rules?

The reliability of data is determined by how often the same information is repeated over a range of different sources. For example, when the results of an experiment are replicated by repeating the experiment under the same conditions, the results are more reliable. Note that reliability is not the same as validity. A result can be reliable without being valid.†

† Validity should probably also be addressed, but it would be much more difficult to enforce.
Should trying to explain things without citing sources be against the rules?

I completely agree with you, but I don't think your suggestion is viable. Citing every fact would create an unreasonable burden on educated contributors. This is made even worse by the fact that some of the most fun things to discuss like quantum mechanics, black holes, and so forth are very high level. Having any sort of discussion would be a sourcing nightmare, and in many cases you likely could not find a precise singular source as you start interweaving knowledge from different fields.

It is indeed a difficult issue. Not to mention the extreme moderation work that would be needed to ensure that the sources are indeed reliable. We have, what, two mods on this sub that are active at all on Voat? A lot more mods would need to be enlisted to ensure that everything goes down well.

And yes, sourcing would be a nightmare. Perhaps only top-level-comments would require sources, and then replies could be sourceless unless asked for by a participant in the discussion or a moderator.
